about: The importer for a pull: it saves what pull() fetched from a hospital as files, and reads them back as documents for an import. It does the same for what a hospital's server said of itself at a connection. cascade-runtime exports pullFiles() and connectFiles() from here; the rest is called by pod.look(), pod.import() and pod.connect().
capabilities: Saving a pull as files · pullFiles()
Refusing a pull an import cannot state · PullRefused, pullFiles(), fhirPull.documents()
Reading a saved pull as documents · fhirPull.documents()
Stating where a pull's records came from · PullDocument.facts()
Listing a saved pull's records before an import · fhirPull.index()
Saving and reading what a hospital's server said of itself · connectFiles(), readConnect(), ConnectRefused

glossary.definition: the instant a hospital answered as of: its records as they stood then, which is not when the document was made or arrived. Only the host that made a demo hospital sets one; a pull from a real hospital has none.
the party that wrote a document's content, such as the hospital whose server gave the record. A document is attributed to its author.
the URL of a hospital's sign-in page, as its server publishes it.
FHIR's resource that holds other resources; a pull keeps everything it fetched in one.
Consolidated Clinical Document Architecture: HL7's standard for the XML summary documents patient portals hand out.
FHIR's resource in which a server says what software it is and what it supports, served at `<FHIR base>/metadata`.
the name a hospital's vendor knows an app by, which the app sends when a person signs in.
one sign-in of one person at one hospital's server. `connect()` returns it as a `Connection`, good for one pull; `pod.connect()` stores the pod's record of it.
the organisation that keeps a document and answers for its true copy.
one file that an import takes whole and gives to an adapter: a FHIR resource or Bundle in JSON, or a C-CDA document. The pod keeps its bytes.
FHIR's resource for a document a hospital holds about a patient, such as a clinical note or a C-CDA document: it points to the document by URL, or carries it inline.
Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources: HL7's standard for health records as JSON.
the URL of a hospital's FHIR server; each record there is at `<FHIR base>/<type>/<id>`.
the part of the runtime that knows one form of export: it says which files are its documents and what the export states about each. `pod.look()` and `pod.import()` try each importer in turn.
one thing `index()` lists for `pod.look()` to count: something an import would bring, with its source's name, its kind or section, and when it was received, each only where the export states it.
the standard name of a file's format, such as `application/fhir+json`; an import offers a document to the adapters of its media type.
the scheme, server name and port of a URL, such as `https://hospital.example`: what a browser treats as one site.
the person an export's records are about, as that source knows them, before anyone has said who they are in the pod.
one person's records, and what that person has said about them, kept as files in one folder.
the records one patient has at one hospital, as `pull()` fetched them in one go, with the FHIR base they came from and when; also the fetching itself.
one thing said about a person's health, such as an allergy, a medication or a lab result.
the vocabulary's class for one kind of record, such as `cascade:LaboratoryTestResult` for a lab result.
one record in FHIR, named by its type and its id, such as `Observation/ldl-1`.
one request to a hospital for a patient's records of one type, such as Condition; a plan lists them, and a hospital may answer a search a page at a time.
what a hospital's server publishes at `<FHIR base>/.well-known/smart-configuration`: where its sign-in page and its token exchange are, and what they support.
one hospital server, or one document, whose records an export holds.
a party that passed a document on without writing it, as Apple Health does with a hospital's records. A document is never attributed to its transmitter.
